fr.elements: Main Residence; Vehicle Parking Area; Detached Structure; Walkway; Open Lawn Area; Dense Vegetation; Access Drive; Water Feature
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Water Feature; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responders can identify it as the only vehicle access point on arrival.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so emergency apparatus can reach the main residence and detached structure without obstruction.
• Designate a flat, open area of the lawn for emergency vehicle staging, away from the water feature.
• Mark the location of the water feature with visible signage or reflective posts so responders moving across the property at night are aware of it.
• Thin the dense vegetation along the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction and responders on foot can move freely alongside them.
• Cut back dense vegetation between the main residence and detached structure to keep a clear path open between the two buildings.
• Trim vegetation along the sides of the walkway so responders can move quickly between structures without pushing through overgrowth.
• Install a gate or marked opening in any rear boundary fence to give responders a secondary on-foot route to the rear of the property.
• Keep any gate on the property unlocked or secured with a Knox-Box or standard breakaway lock so responders are not delayed gaining access.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Terrain; Grass Cover; Water Feature; Multiple Access Routes; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster to reduce the amount of closely spaced trees that could carry fire toward the structure.
• Trim branches on scattered trees so the lowest limbs are well above the ground.
• Cut back shrubs and plants that are growing directly against or touching the structure.
• Mow or cut grass cover around the structure regularly, especially during dry periods.
• Keep the area between the tree cluster and the structure as open as possible by removing any shrubs or plants filling that gap.
• Keep all access routes clear of overhanging branches and overgrown vegetation along the edges.
• Maintain the open terrain areas around the structure by preventing shrubs or small trees from establishing in those spaces.
